title: Settlement subscription delay
telemetry: Protected synthetic export combines supplied Cloud Monitoring subscription observations, subscriber application records and a settlement-owner effect sample. The subscription is global; us-central1 identifies its subscriber deployment. The fixture CLI returns this labelled packet, not a native multi-service query result.
owner: Morgan, Settlements on-call, owns the investigation. The subscriber application owner owns code and capacity decisions; the settlement ledger owner reconciles effects. ITO coordinates the existing TLC and change approvals.
task: Morgan has asked you to investigate delayed settlement posting for settlement-posting-sub in synthetic-settlements-prod. Review the available observations for 2026-10-09 09:00-09:12 UTC and return a bounded technical finding with the supporting evidence, remaining unknowns and the next useful check with its owner. The existing TLC is the coordination channel. No change is approved.

sources.claim: Pub/Sub topics and subscriptions have a global namespace and are not tied to a particular region. The regional field here scopes the synthetic subscriber deployment; it does not assert a regional subscription or data-residency guarantee.

Rising backlog and oldest unacknowledged age require subscriber investigation; repeated negative acknowledgments can redeliver the same message. Metric growth alone does not distinguish insufficient processing capacity from message-specific failures.
Pub/Sub retries delivery when a subscriber cannot acknowledge a message. Retrying delivery does not itself establish whether an application side effect already completed.
The pubsub_subscription resource has project_id and subscription_id labels; the fixture region identifies the consumer deployment rather than a regional subscription.

a.conclusion: The observed subscriber processing capacity is below the arrival rate: four occupied handlers complete about 200 messages per minute against 400 arriving. The sampled acknowledgment and effect evidence supports a throughput bottleneck, not a repeated poison-message mechanism.
next_checks: The subscriber owner checks handler time, effective concurrency, resource saturation and safe capacity headroom for this workload before proposing a bounded capacity change.
Morgan and the ledger owner track unique completed effects, backlog and age over subsequent complete intervals; any recovery claim requires sustained useful throughput and declining delay.
The ledger owner reconciles effect IDs before any separately approved replay; no replay is needed merely to diagnose the backlog.
unsupported: Calling this a poison-message or acknowledgment failure despite the supplied saturated-handler evidence.
Promising a particular scale factor will recover the backlog without measuring downstream limits.
Claiming no duplicate effects exist throughout the backlog from the small sample or replaying blindly.
unknowns: Why the current subscriber capacity was selected and whether downstream capacity permits an increase.
The complete effect history and current state after 09:12 UTC.

b.conclusion: Repeated negative acknowledgments of unsupported schemaVersion=7 messages consume deliveries while valid version-6 messages succeed. The sampled idle capacity and low CPU contradict a simple insufficient-worker explanation; the incompatibility is observed, but its introduction and full effect history remain unknown.
next_checks: The subscriber and publisher owners compare the agreed schema contract and when version-7 messages began, using sanitized metadata without consuming or acknowledging additional messages.
The ledger owner reconciles all affected effect IDs before owners select an approved retry, compatibility repair or disposition; do not discard or replay messages by default.
Morgan watches unique completion rate, repeated IDs, age and backlog after an owner-approved repair.
unsupported: Diagnosing insufficient CPU or worker count as the demonstrated cause and scaling as the fix.
Treating a nack as proof the side effect is absent for every message or using repeated nacks as a discard mechanism.
Declaring all settlements safe, replaying the subscription, seeking, or acknowledging failed messages.
unknowns: Which publisher change introduced schemaVersion=7 and the full set of affected messages.
Whether other delivered messages already have effects and whether a particular recovery policy is safe.

The observed zero nack/expiry/failure counters and distinct-ID sample do not support poison-message redelivery as this case's explanation; they do not prove exactly-once effects.
